project.name: PcapPlusPlus

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42530090 (PcapPlusPlus): Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 2 found by fuzz target FuzzTarget [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42530090
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source / static parse of the staged poc
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced an AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 2 in `pcpp::GREv1Layer::computeCalculateFields()` at `Packet++/src/GreLayer.cpp:542`. A static parse of the staged `poc` shows a raw-IP pcap whose first packet has `incl_len == 25` and packet bytes `45 11 70 ff 64 77 80 00 6e 2f 91 16 df fd 93 62 e9 00 f6 00 00 21 65 80 00`. The IPv4 header consumes 20 bytes and its protocol byte is `0x2f` (GRE), so `IPv4Layer::parseNextLayer()` materializes the final five bytes `00 21 65 80 00` as the GRE payload. `GreLayer::getGREVersion()` only requires `sizeof(gre_basic_header)` (4 bytes), so it classifies that 5-byte slice as GREv1 from the low version bits of `0x21`. The vulnerable IPv4 GRE branch then constructs `GREv1Layer` with those five bytes and no `payloadLen >= sizeof(gre1_header)` check. On the witness all GRE optional-bit flags are clear, so GRE header-length calculation leaves only one payload byte beyond the 4-byte basic GRE header; the mandatory `gre1_header::payloadLength` and `callID` fields do not actually fit. When the harness later calls `parsedPacket.computeCalculateFields()`, `GREv1Layer::computeCalculateFields()` still writes the 2-byte `payloadLength` field at offset 4, beginning on the last byte of the 25-byte raw packet allocation and overrunning one byte past it. The staged fix adds `GREv0Layer::isDataValid()` / `GREv1Layer::isDataValid()` and requires those checks before constructing GRE layers from IPv4 or IPv6 payloads, so short GRE inputs fall back to `PayloadLayer` instead of being reserialized as GREv1.

source.description: First project statement on the vulnerable path that materializes the attacker-controlled GRE byte slice and its length from the raw IPv4 packet tail.
source.value_from: A static parse of `gt_results/arvo_42530090/poc` shows first-packet `incl_len == 25` and raw packet bytes `45 11 70 ff 64 77 80 00 6e 2f 91 16 df fd 93 62 e9 00 f6 00 00 21 65 80 00`. The IPv4 IHL nibble `5` makes `hdrLen == 20`, and the protocol byte `0x2f` routes into GRE parsing, so the final five bytes `00 21 65 80 00` become the `payload` / `payloadLen == 5` pair created here.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `GREv1Layer::computeCalculateFields()` writes the 2-byte `payloadLength` field through `getGreHeader()` even though the layer only aliases a 5-byte GRE slice.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 2` at this exact line and says the target address is 0 bytes to the right of the 25-byte heap region allocated in `pcpp::PcapFileReaderDevice::getNextPacket()`.

root_cause.code:
else if (greVer == GREv1)
    m_NextLayer = new GREv1Layer(payload, payloadLen, this, m_Packet);
root_cause.description: Root cause. Once GRE version probing says `GREv1`, IPv4 parsing constructs a `GREv1Layer` from the same 5-byte slice without validating that the buffer is large enough for `sizeof(gre1_header)`.
root_cause.note: The staged patch changes this branch to `else if (greVer == GREv1 && GREv1Layer::isDataValid(payload, payloadLen))`, and `GREv1Layer::isDataValid()` requires at least `sizeof(gre1_header)` (8) bytes. The witness satisfies the old 4-byte version probe but not the fixed 8-byte constructor precondition.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant attacker-controlled state is the GRE payload pointer and its 5-byte extent. These lines derive that exact slice from the raw IPv4 packet.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: On the staged witness the last five raw packet bytes are `00 21 65 80 00`, so this code materializes `payload` over those bytes and `payloadLen == 5`.

parser_admitted.description: After the pcap packet has already been admitted as IPv4, the IPv4 protocol field `47` sends execution into the GRE branch and begins GRE-specific parsing on the final five packet bytes. The saved stdout confirms this path with `IPv4 Layer, Src: 223.253.147.98, Dst: 233.0.246.0` followed by `GRE Layer, version 1`.

coarse_trace.summary: IPv4 parsing slices the final five packet bytes as GRE and version probing accepts them as GREv1 using only the 4-byte basic GRE header.
The GRE branch constructs a `GREv1Layer` over those five bytes with no `sizeof(gre1_header)` validation; the staged patch adds this exact missing check.
GRE header-length calculation leaves only one payload byte beyond the 4-byte basic GRE header, proving the mandatory GREv1 `payloadLength` and `callID` fields do not fit in the backing bytes.
Packet recalculation later writes the GREv1 `payloadLength` field through that truncated layer and overruns the 25-byte raw packet allocation with the saved 2-byte heap write.

fine_trace.note: Source. For the 25-byte raw-IP witness, `getHeaderLen()` returns 20 from the IPv4 IHL nibble `0x5`, so these lines materialize the final five packet bytes `00 21 65 80 00` as `payload` and set `payloadLen = 5`.

This version probe is the only present admission check before GREv1 construction. Because step 1 produced `payloadLen = 5`, the `greDataLen < sizeof(gre_basic_header)` guard passes, and the low three bits of `payload[1]` (`0x21`) decode as version `1`, so the short buffer is classified as GREv1 using only the 4-byte basic header.

fine_trace.code:
else if (greVer == GREv1)
    m_NextLayer = new GREv1Layer(payload, payloadLen, this, m_Packet);
fine_trace.note: Root cause. Once step 2 returns `GREv1`, IPv4 parsing constructs a `GREv1Layer` over the same five bytes without checking that `payloadLen` is large enough for `sizeof(gre1_header)` (8). The fixed code adds `GREv1Layer::isDataValid(payload, payloadLen)` here, which would reject this witness and fall back to `PayloadLayer`.

On the 5-byte GREv1 object from step 3, `getHeaderLen()` resolves to 4 because the first GRE bytes leave checksum, routing, key, sequence, and ack bits clear. That leaves only `payloadLen = 1`, matching the saved stdout line `Payload Layer, Data length: 1 [Bytes]`; the mandatory `gre1_header::payloadLength` and `callID` fields therefore do not fit in the layer backing bytes.

Sink. After the harness calls `parsedPacket.computeCalculateFields()`, `Packet::computeCalculateFields()` revisits the malformed GREv1 layer from step 3 and this store writes the 2-byte `payloadLength` field at offset 4 of `gre1_header`. With `m_DataLen = 5` and step 4 showing only one byte exists beyond the 4-byte basic GRE header, the store begins on the last byte of the 25-byte raw packet allocation and overruns one byte past it, matching ASan's `heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 2` at this exact line.

allocation_context.note: ASan says the crashing 25-byte heap region was created by `new uint8_t[pkthdr.caplen]` at this line.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the crash by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42530090 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which produced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 2` in `pcpp::GREv1Layer::computeCalculateFields()`.

format.name: raw-IP pcap with truncated GREv1 payload
format.contract: A raw-IP pcap whose first packet is 25 bytes long: a 20-byte IPv4 header with protocol `47` (GRE) followed by exactly the five GRE bytes `00 21 65 80 00`. Those bytes satisfy `GreLayer::getGREVersion()` as GREv1 but do not satisfy the fixed `GREv1Layer::isDataValid(payload, payloadLen)` requirement of at least `sizeof(gre1_header)` bytes, so `GREv1Layer::computeCalculateFields()` later overwrites the missing 2-byte `payloadLength` field. The staged artifacts only prove this exact 5-byte short-GRE witness and do not justify a broader trigger contract.
